attacks.reason: The internal ribbing may not provide sufficient mechanical interlock to counteract cyclic masticatory forces.
attacks.evidence_required: Finite element analysis or experimental testing to validate the mechanical interlock of the internal ribbing.

attacks.reason: The transfer from 3D printing to mechanical interlock is not clearly justified.
attacks.evidence_required: A clear explanation of the relationship between 3D printing and mechanical interlock is required.

attacks.reason: The inventive device fails under high cyclic masticatory forces, which may exceed the material's yield strength.
attacks.evidence_required: Experimental testing to determine the material's yield strength under cyclic masticatory forces.

attacks.reason: An expert in the field would naturally combine 3D printing with internal ribbing to enhance mechanical interlock.
attacks.evidence_required: A clear explanation of the non-obvious combination of 3D printing and internal ribbing is required.

attacks.reason: Existing references disclose similar uses of 3D printing to enhance mechanical interlock.
attacks.evidence_required: A thorough search of prior art to identify similar uses of 3D printing to enhance mechanical interlock.

attacks.reason: The 3D printing process may not be able to accurately replicate the internal ribbing pattern.
attacks.evidence_required: Experimental testing to validate the accuracy of the 3D printing process in replicating the internal ribbing pattern.

attacks.reason: The inventive device's performance cannot be reliably measured under controlled conditions.
attacks.evidence_required: A clear explanation of how the inventive device's performance can be reliably measured under controlled conditions is required.

refinement_needed: A clear explanation of the non-obvious combination of 3D printing and internal ribbing, and a thorough search of prior art to identify similar uses of 3D printing to enhance mechanical interlock.
